answer: Pay each epoch as a zero-sum tournament. Verifiable randomness sorts identities into groups, each splitting one fixed pot by contribution; the pot never grows with headcount. Ten clones then compete for one identity's coins, yet pay ten sets of fees, so splitting adds cost with zero marginal gain. Since the shuffle is unknowable in advance, a farm cannot scatter puppets across pots. A lone sparrow earns its share, but the velvet dream of endless accounts meets a hard horizon: self-dealing only recycles one operator's own stake. Sybils lose by construction, not detection.
